overview.text: Today's developments showcase notable advancements across model architectures, open-weight releases, and driving world models. SO-Arena introduces benchmarks evaluating the capability spectrum and reliability of System One models, while a separate study explores transferring LLMs into efficient System One models via adaptive computation. In generative models, BirdDreams presents joint perspective and BEV video generation for reactive driving world models, and Duo v1 introduces a reciprocal world model for full-duplex audiovisual interaction. Additionally, G-STAR addresses token capacity trade-offs in deeply compressed autoregressive image generation. Open-weight releases like Edge0-145B bring frontier AI capabilities to local hardware, and models such as thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small and ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview continue to drive community experimentation. These updates collectively highlight ongoing efforts to improve model efficiency, interactive perception, and local deployment options for researchers and developers.

entries.title: SO-Arena: Benchmarking the Capability Spectrum and Reliability of System One Models
entries.summary: System One models promise fast, general-purpose decision-making without lengthy token generation. However, understanding their capability spectrum and decision reliability requires more than aggregate performance on current benchmarks.
entries.why: Provides essential evaluation standards for understanding reliability and capability spectra in fast System One models.

entries.title: The avalanche that hit math is coming for AI development
entries.summary: If you asked me earlier this year how far away we are from superintelligence, I’d probably have said at least the better part of a decade. But over the last three months, from debating people on and off the podcast, I’ve updated my views a ton.
entries.why: Offers valuable perspective shifts on timelines and developments toward advanced artificial intelligence systems.

entries.title: Edge0-145B: Frontier AI Capabilities on Your Own Computer
entries.why: Brings frontier-level capabilities directly to local hardware setups for independent developers and researchers.

entries.title: BirdDreams: Joint Perspective and BEV Video Generation for a Plausible, Reactive Driving World Model
entries.summary: Driving world models aim to simulate how a scene unfolds under different ego actions. This requires plausible motion of surrounding vehicles as well as precise ego-trajectory control.
entries.why: Advances reactive driving world models through joint perspective and BEV video generation techniques.

entries.title: Duo: A Reciprocal World Model for Full-Duplex Interaction
entries.summary: In this report, we introduce the Reciprocal World Model (RWM) and present Duo v1, a full-duplex world model that continuously perceives audiovisual inputs while responding to users in real time.
entries.why: Enables real-time, full-duplex audiovisual interaction using a novel reciprocal world model architecture.

entries.title: G-STAR: Group-Scaled Token Capacity for Deeply Compressed Autoregressive Generation
entries.summary: Discrete autoregressive models offer a scalable framework for image generation. However, they face a fundamental trade-off: long token sequences preserve representation quality but slow generation, while aggressive spatial compression reduces representation capacity.
entries.why: Tackles the fundamental trade-off between representation quality and generation speed in autoregressive image models.

entries.title: From Large Language Models to Efficient System One Models via Adaptive Computation
entries.summary: Transferring LLMs into System One decision models typically replaces the language modeling head with a decision head while retaining the full backbone, making every decision pay for all layers. Yet it remains unclear how much depth such decisions require.
entries.why: Investigates how much depth is required when transferring large language models into efficient decision-making architectures.
